plan.contextChunk: This figure sets four triangle sketches in a row, labeled (a) through (d) below, to enumerate the possible outcomes when two sides and a non-included angle are known. All four share one labeling scheme: an acute angle alpha marked by an arc at the left end of a horizontal base, a vertex beta at the right end of that base, an apex gamma above, side b rising from alpha to gamma, and side a hanging from gamma. Panel (a), headed No triangle, a < h, draws a as a short vertical segment from gamma that stops above the base, leaving a visible gap so nothing closes. Panel (b), headed Right triangle, a = h, has a reaching the base exactly at beta, with a small square marking the right angle formed there. Panel (c), headed Two triangles, a > h, a < b, shows a solid vertical altitude labeled h from gamma to the base, plus two dashed segments each labeled a running from gamma to different landing points, one to the left of the altitude's foot and one at beta. Panel (d), headed One triangle, a is greater than or equal to b, shows a broad triangle whose side a slopes from gamma down to beta. Aligning the four under identical labels isolates the one quantity that changes, the length of a measured against the altitude and against b, and shows how many closures each case admits.

interactionPlan.concept: In the ambiguous case (SSA) of a triangle, the length of the opposite side a compared to the altitude h and adjacent side b determines whether 0, 1, or 2 triangles can be formed.
elements: fixed vertex alpha at the left with an angle arc
fixed horizontal base ray extending to the right from alpha
fixed side b extending upward and rightward from alpha to apex gamma
altitude line h dropping vertically from gamma to the base ray, with a right-angle marker
dynamic side a swinging from apex gamma toward the base ray
vertex beta marking the intersection(s) of side a and the base ray
labels for angles (alpha, beta, gamma) and sides (a, b, h)
dynamic text label indicating the current case (e.g., 'Two triangles, a > h, a < b')

interactions.label: Length of side a
interactions.teaches: As side a grows, it transitions from being too short to reach the base, to perfectly grazing it, to intersecting it twice, to reaching far enough to form just one triangle.

interactions.label: Altitude reference
interactions.teaches: The altitude h is the shortest possible distance from the apex to the base, serving as the absolute minimum length side a must have to close the triangle.

demo_steps.title: No triangle
demo_steps.narration: When side a is shorter than the altitude h, it cannot reach the base at all. The triangle cannot close.

demo_steps.title: Right triangle
demo_steps.narration: When side a exactly equals the altitude h, it meets the base at exactly one perpendicular point, forming a single right triangle.

demo_steps.title: Two triangles
demo_steps.narration: When side a is longer than h but shorter than b, it can swing to intersect the base at two distinct points, creating two valid triangle geometries.

demo_steps.title: One triangle
demo_steps.narration: When side a is equal to or longer than b, swinging it to the left would cross outside the fixed angle alpha, so it only forms one valid triangle on the right.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The altitude h sets the absolute minimum length needed to close the triangle, while side b sets the threshold beyond which the 'inner' second triangle becomes impossible.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Create a single interactive diagram that dynamically updates based on the slider, replacing the 4 static panels. Fix angle alpha (e.g., 30 degrees) and side b (e.g., length 10), so h = 5. Slider values dictate the geometry: when a < 5, draw a segment hanging from gamma with a visible gap. When a = 5, draw a single vertical segment to the base. When 5 < a < 10, draw two dashed segments for a intersecting the base at two different points. When a >= 10, draw a single solid segment for a intersecting the base to the right. The toggle shows/hides a dashed vertical line for h and its right-angle marker.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for side length a: the learner drags the candidate side a while alpha and b stay fixed, the construction passes through no triangle, right triangle, two triangles, and one triangle, showing that the number of possible closures depends on comparing a with h and b.
- Toggle for showing altitude h: the learner turns the altitude guide on or off, the threshold line and right-angle marker appear across the panels, making clear why a below h cannot reach the base and a equal to h gives exactly one right triangle.
- Button/state for case stepping: the learner advances through the four named cases one at a time, the active panel highlights its closing side or gap, connecting each inequality for a to the visible geometric outcome.

authoredContext:
Oblique triangles in the category SSA may have four different outcomes. The figure illustrates the solutions with the known sides a and b and known angle α.

Four attempted oblique triangles are in a row, all with standard labels. Side c is the horizontal base. In the first attempted triangle, side a is less than the altitude height. Since side a cannot reach side c, there is no triangle. In the second attempted triangle, side a is equal to the length of the altitude height, so side a forms a right angle with side c. In the third attempted triangle, side a is greater than the altitude height and less than side b, so side a can form either an acute or obtuse angle with side c. In the fourth attempted triangle, side a is greater than or equal to side b, so side a forms an acute angle with side c.

discrepancies: The α angle label is placed outside and to the left of the vertex, whereas the source places it inside the angle arc.
In the "Right triangle" case (b), the generated code draws the right-angle square marker on the outside (right) of the vertical line, whereas the source draws it on the inside (left).
In the "Two triangles" case (c) of the source, the altitude h is drawn as a solid line, but the generated figure draws it as a dashed line.
The generated figure defaults to showing the altitude in cases (a) and (d) where the source figure originally omitted it.
evaluation.notes: The generated interactive figure is an excellent pedagogical adaptation of the four static source panels, accurately demonstrating the ambiguous case of the Law of Sines with a slider and step player, marred only by a few minor label and drawing alignment issues.
action_items: Move the 'α' label to the right of the vertex (e.g., A_x + 15) so it sits inside the angle arc, matching the source.
Change the right-angle path in the `a === h_val` condition to draw on the left side of the vertical line (using C_x - 12) so it correctly sits inside the triangle.
Change the altitude line stroke from dashed to solid, matching the source's 'Two triangles' panel.
Update the default state of the `show_alt` toggle in the `steps` array so it is only true in the 'Two triangles' step, mirroring the source's visibility choices.
